newsitem.title: USA: Talked to your e-mail recently? Now you can.
newsitem.headline: Talked to your e-mail recently? Now you can.

text.p: If you've ever had the urge to check your e-mail messages from the road without having to carry a bulky computer, Millennia Software Inc. may have just the product for you.

The Saratoga, Calif., startup plans to launch its first product, Email Reader, on Monday at a price of $89.95. The software enables you to use a standard telephone, mobile phone or payphone to have your e-mail messages read to you.
Email Reader runs on personal computers equipped with Intel Corp. Pentium microprocessors, Microsoft Corp.'s Windows 95 operating system, and a voice modem.
Based on AT&T Corp.'s Watson voice processing technology and Millenia's own patent-pending VoiceLINK software engine, Email Reader will be available via toll-free telephone or over the Internet.

"We focused on e-mail because that's really an area that is critical to the mobile professional," said Royce Johnson, vice president of marketing at Millenia. He noted the product is aimed especially at mobile small- and home-office workers.

Millenia's VoiceLINK engine converts a set of more than a dozen pre-determined spoken commands into digital instructions that a computer can understand. A voice synthesizer reads the e-mail messages back according to a caller's instructions.
Initially, the software requires a 75-megahertz Pentium or above and 16 megabytes of random access memory, or RAM.

It currently is set up to read back messages and to execute simple playback and marking commands. But the company is also developing products that can handle languages other than English, and can answer e-mail with pre-set responses.

The first version will work only on stand-alone computers with standard e-mail such as Euroda, POP3, and that from Microsoft and Netscape Communications Corp. But future releases will handle network and on-line mail as well.
The product is the first of a generation of offerings based on VoiceLINK, which could eventually include paging, faxing and personal information management applications.
Millenia was founded in 1995 by two former Intel engineers with financial backing from AT&T Corp., as well as individual investors.
